rav1e.install:
%cargo_install
cargo cinstall %(options_cargo_release) \
               --destdir=%(installroot) \
               --prefix=%(prefix) \
               --libdir=%(libdir)

# KILL IT WITH FIRE
rm -v %(installroot)/%(libdir)/*.a

rclone.build:
%make TAG=v%(version) GOTAGS=noselfupdate

./rclone genautocomplete bash rclone.bash_completion
./rclone genautocomplete zsh rclone.zsh_completion
./rclone genautocomplete fish rclone.fish_completion
rclone.install:
%install_bin rclone

# Mount helper symlinks
%install_dir %(installroot)%(sbindir)
ln -srv %(installroot)%(bindir)/rclone %(installroot)%(sbindir)/mount.rclone
ln -srv %(installroot)%(bindir)/rclone %(installroot)%(sbindir)/rclonefs

%install_file rclone.bash_completion %(installroot)%(bashcompletionsdir)/rclone
%install_file rclone.zsh_completion %(installroot)%(zshcompletionsdir)/_rclone
%install_file rclone.fish_completion %(installroot)%(fishcompletionsdir)/rclone.fish

%install_file rclone.1 -t %(installroot)%(mandir)/man1

re2.check:
# %cmake_test's --verbose floods the container log with the exhaustive tests'
# progress output; run ctest quietly and only show output for failures.
ctest --test-dir %(builddir) --output-on-failure --parallel %(jobs) --force-new-ctest-process

readline.install:
%make_install

# Empty
rmdir -v %(installroot)%(bindir)

# Not useful
rm -rfv %(installroot)%(docdir)/readline/
rmdir -v %(installroot)%(docdir)/

ripgrep.install:
%cargo_install rg

# completions
%(cargo_target_dir)/rg --generate complete-bash | %install_file /dev/stdin %(installroot)%(bashcompletionsdir)/rg
%(cargo_target_dir)/rg --generate complete-fish | %install_file /dev/stdin %(installroot)%(fishcompletionsdir)/rg.fish
%(cargo_target_dir)/rg --generate complete-zsh | %install_file /dev/stdin %(installroot)%(zshcompletionsdir)/_rg

# man pages
%(cargo_target_dir)/rg --generate man | %install_file /dev/stdin %(installroot)%(mandir)/man1/rg.1

roswell.setup:
sh bootstrap
%configure \
    --prefix=%(prefix) \
    --sysconfdir=%(vendordir) # TODO: stateless. Could not figure out how to make a stateless patch so this is the best option for now. If someone else wants to tackle it be my guest.

subpackages.description:
The rsync daemon, which serves directory trees over the rsync://
protocol, and its systemd units.

rrsync confines rsync to a single directory when used as an SSH forced
command, so a remote peer can push or pull files there without getting
general shell access.

rtkit.install:
%meson_install

# userdb pls
%install_file %(pkgdir)/rtkit.group %(installroot)%(libdir)/userdb/rtkit.group
ln -s rtkit.group %(installroot)%(libdir)/userdb/133.group
%install_file %(pkgdir)/rtkit.user %(installroot)%(libdir)/userdb/rtkit.user

rm -v %(installroot)%(sysusersdir)/rtkit.conf

ruby.setup:
export LDFLAGS="$(echo ${LDFLAGS} | sed --expression='s/-Wl,--icf=safe //')"

%configure \
    --disable-rpath \
    --enable-shared \
    --with-sitedir=%(libdir)/ruby/site_ruby \
    --disable-install-doc \
    --with-ruby-version="${major_version}.${minor_version}"
## TODO: Figure out why docs won't build (the --disable-install-doc flag above)
ruby.install:
%make_install

# Remove unreproducible files
rm -fvr %(installroot)/usr/lib/ruby/gems/${major_version}.${minor_version}/cache

# Provide an unversioned pkgconfig so we don't need to update it in revdeps when doing a major update
ln -s ruby-${major_version}.${minor_version}.pc %(installroot)/%(libdir)/pkgconfig/ruby.pc

# Delete any empty directories to prevent path conflicts
find %(installroot) -type d -empty -print -delete

runc.setup:
mkdir -p src/github.com/opencontainers/runc/
find ./* -prune ! -name src -exec mv {} src/github.com/opencontainers/runc/ \;
runc.build:
export GOPATH="${PWD}"
export BUILDTAGS='seccomp'
export GOFLAGS="-trimpath -mod=readonly -modcacherw"
export CGO_CFLAGS="${CFLAGS}"

# Git SHA corresponding to the release tag
export COMMIT=$(git ls-remote https://github.com/opencontainers/runc.git refs/tags/v%(version)^{} |awk '{print $1}')

cd src/github.com/opencontainers/runc/
%make runc man

rust.setup:
# Ensure that we use the system sqlite3
%patch %(pkgdir)/0001-unbundle-sqlite.patch -d src/tools/cargo
find ./vendor/libsqlite3-sys*/sqlite3/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print

# Remove unused vendored libraries
find ./vendor/curl-sys*/curl/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print
find ./vendor/libffi-sys*/libffi/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print
find ./vendor/libssh2-sys*/libssh2/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print
find ./vendor/libz-sys*/src/zlib{,-ng}/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print
find ./vendor/openssl-src*/openssl/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print
find ./vendor/libgit2-sys*/libgit2/ -mindepth 1 -delete -print

# Fix bootstrap checking checksums for all the files we just deleted
find vendor -name .cargo-checksum.json -print \
    -exec sed -i.uncheck -e 's/"files":{[^}]*}/"files":{ }/' '{}' '+'

%patch %(pkgdir)/ldd-default.patch
%patch %(pkgdir)/libdir.patch
rust.build:
LLVM_VERSION=$(${LLVM_CONFIG} --version)
LLVM_MAJOR="$( cut -d '.' -f 1 <<< "${LLVM_VERSION}" )"
LLVM_LIBDIR=$(${LLVM_CONFIG} --libdir)
COMPILER_RT_DIR="${LLVM_LIBDIR}/clang/${LLVM_MAJOR}/lib/linux"

if [[ " ${PATH[*]} " =~ "ccache" ]]; then
    CCACHE_ENABLE="true"
else
    CCACHE_ENABLE="false"
fi

# build.full-bootstrap=true is necessary to force the build to use the stage 1 rustc to build a stage 2 libstd. We need that for profiling data
# We want some kind of lto enabled so that we get profiling data from it, and thin-lto is much faster to build than full lto.
python ./x.py build \
    --build-dir %(workdir)/build-pgo \
    --config %(pkgdir)/config.toml \
    --jobs %(jobs) \
    --set build.ccache=${CCACHE_ENABLE} \
    --set build.full-bootstrap=true \
    --set rust.lto=thin-local \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.llvm-config="${LLVM_CONFIG}" \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.optimized-compiler-builtins="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.builtins-i386.a" \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.profiler="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.profile-i386.a" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.llvm-config="${LLVM_CONFIG}" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.optimized-compiler-builtins="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.builtins-x86_64.a" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.profiler="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.profile-x86_64.a" \
    --rust-profile-generate %(workdir)/rustc-pgo-profile-data \
    --stage 2

${LLVM_PROFDATA} merge -output=%(workdir)/rustc-pgo-profile-data/rustc-pgo.profdata %(workdir)/rustc-pgo-profile-data/default_*.profraw

# rust-bootstrap is very inconsistent with the stages of various tools that it wants to build between `dist` and `install`. This
# causes a lot of redundant and unnecessary builds if we attempt to do the build with various stages (IE build the compiler first, then the
# tools, then install it last). To prevent this from happening just let `install` figure out what it wants.
DESTDIR=%(installroot) python3 x.py install \
    --build-dir %(workdir)/build-release \
    --config %(pkgdir)/config.toml \
    --jobs %(jobs) \
    --set build.ccache=${CCACHE_ENABLE} \
    --set build.full-bootstrap=false \
    --set rust.lto=fat \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.llvm-config="${LLVM_CONFIG}" \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.optimized-compiler-builtins="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.builtins-i386.a" \
    --set target.i686-unknown-linux-gnu.profiler="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.profile-i386.a" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.llvm-config="${LLVM_CONFIG}" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.optimized-compiler-builtins="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.builtins-x86_64.a" \
    --set target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.profiler="${COMPILER_RT_DIR}/libclang_rt.profile-x86_64.a" \
    --rust-profile-use %(workdir)/rustc-pgo-profile-data/rustc-pgo.profdata
rust.install:
install -Dm00644 %(installroot)/etc/bash_completion.d/* -t %(installroot)/usr/share/bash-completion/completions
rm -rvf %(installroot)/etc

# Remove text files from libs (manifests, installation logs...)
find %(installroot)/%(libdir)/rustlib -maxdepth 1 -type f -delete -print
rust.environment:
# Don't set these here, all configuration should come from config.toml or the package.yml
unset RUSTFLAGS

# Force use of libsqlite3, libgit2, and libssh2 system libs
export LIBSQLITE3_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG=1
export LIBSSH2_SYS_USE_PKG_CONFIG=1
export LIBGIT2_NO_VENDOR=1
export RUSTONIG_SYSTEM_LIBONIG=1

# Todo: Figure out how to link this against a dynamic libjemalloc
export JEMALLOC_OVERRIDE=%(libdir)/libjemalloc.a

# This needs to match which llvm we're building against. This should generally be `/usr/bin/llvm-config` but if we're using a versioned
# package that will need to point to the versioned llvm-config
LLVM_CONFIG=%(bindir)/llvm-config-23
LLVM_PROFDATA=%(bindir)/llvm-profdata-23
